title: selector-normalization-probe-suite-wip
summary: Working probe-suite for exercising function/tool selector behavior when prompts include noisy or non-canonical arguments. Focus areas: argument normalization, reroute policies, multi-step handoffs, and graceful fallback to default tools.
purpose: Create a compact, reproducible set of prompts and pass/fail heuristics that surface regressions in selector accuracy and argument-parsing fidelity when onboarding new LLM versions or tokenizer/quantization changes.
scope: Short-form prompts (1-4 turns) and two-step flows that exercise: (1) tool selection between overlapping tools, (2) parsing of ambiguous args (dates, locations, IDs), (3) normalization hooks (units, casing, punctuation), (4) fallback decisions (use default vs ask clarifying question).
test_matrix: Dimensions covered: model variant (base, quantized-8, gpt-style), sequence length bucket (short, medium), presence of prefix cache, routing policy (latency-first, cost-first), and decision threshold for selector probability. Each combination will run 200 seeds of paraphrases sampled from the prompt set.
sample_prompts: User: Schedule a meeting next Friday at 2 with the infra team. -> Expected: select calendar.create_event(tool) with args {date: YYYY-MM-DD normalized, time: 14:00}
User: Can you find the order for order# 4,567? -> Expected: select order.lookup with args {order_id: 4567 (digits only)}
User: What's the weather in 'nyc' tomorrow morning? -> Expected: select weather.query with args {location: New York, NY, date: YYYY-MM-DD, timeframe: morning}
User: Translate to Spanish: "Hello! How are you?" -> Expected: select translation.simple with args {target_lang: es}

User: Convert 5kgs to lbs and add to the recipe -> Expected: detect two-step intent: (1) unit.convert value 5 kg -> 11.0231 lb, (2) recipe.add ingredient '11.0231 lb' and choose appropriate toolchain with preservation of precision
evaluation_criteria: Primary signal: correct tool selected (binary). Secondary signals: argument canonicalization accuracy (string match on normalized form), whether clarifying question was asked when threshold below configured value, and whether multi-step chaining preserved arg fidelity across steps.
baseline_results: Baseline run (model:v2024-09-base) on 10k prompts: tool_selection_accuracy=0.92, arg_normalization_f1=0.87, clarify_rate=0.06, chain_preservation_rate=0.88. Quantized-8 variants show 2-3% drop on arg_normalization especially for punctuation-heavy IDs.
quick_checks: Smoke checks to run on every model pull: (1) 50 paraphrase variance prompts for numeric IDs, (2) 50 unit-conversion chaintests, (3) 30 ambiguous-location prompts. Fail-fast if any regression_triggers fired.
observability_hooks: Emit per-request: chosen_tool, selector_confidence, normalized_args_blob (string), clarifying_question_flag, step_id for chains. Tag runs with model_commit and quantization_profile. Surface in per-route dashboard with per-bucket breakdowns.
known_edge_cases: Abbreviated city names (e.g., 'sf', 'stl') mapping to multiple canonical locations; order numbers containing punctuation or leading zeros; mixed-metric inputs like '5kg 300g'; user shorthand like 'tmrw' for tomorrow.
annotations_guidelines: Labelers should provide: canonicalized args, chosen_tool, and a short rationale. For multi-step flows annotate step boundaries and expected outputs for each step. Use standard tokenization preview to help with quantization-related failures.
quick_examples_for_oncall: If a rollout causes selector_accuracy drop, check selector_confidence histogram and sample requests where confidence between 0.4-0.7; inspect normalized_args_blob for truncation or tokenization artifacts; if quantized build is suspect, re-run smoke on base model and quantized build with identical seeds.
next_steps: 1) Expand paraphrase set by +2k examples focusing on punctuation-heavy IDs. 2) Add automated CI gate that fails PRs if any regression_triggers fire on the smoke suite. 3) Ship an internal dashboard widget that surfaces the top 10 failing canonicalizations with examples.
notes: This doc is intentionally compact — treat as a playground and checklist for onboarding new model builds. We aim to convert the best failing examples into a persistent corpus for long-term regression tracking.
